expected_issues: SQL injection via string interpolation in query - user input is directly embedded in SQL without parameterization

Race condition: concurrent calls to process() can cause cache corruption since fetchData reads and writes the shared cache without synchronization, and multiple in-flight fetches for the same id can overwrite each other

Resource leak: stream is never explicitly closed on error - the error handler logs but does not destroy the stream or reject the promise, leaving the file descriptor open and the caller hanging on a never-resolved promise
Hardcoded secrets: database password, JWT secret, and Stripe live API key are embedded directly in source code. These should be loaded from environment variables or a secrets manager.

Off-by-one error: the function uses 0-based page indexing but the comment and typical API convention expects 1-based pages. paginate(items, 1, 10) returns items at indices 10-19 (the second page), but callers likely expect page 1 to return the first 10 items

Missing null check: if userRepo.findById returns null (user not found), accessing user.name will throw TypeError. Similarly, user.profile could be null/undefined, causing a crash when accessing avatarUrl

Insecure deserialization: the endpoint deserializes arbitrary data from an external webhook without validation. If deserialize() uses eval, Function constructor, or reconstructs arbitrary class instances, an attacker can achieve remote code execution. The base64 payload is also parsed without input validation or signature verification.
